name: Vergelegen

dates.altered: Altered by Samuel Kerr in the nineteenth century; restored, refurbished and extended for Lady Florence Phillips from 1922 by the architect Percy Walgate, who produced 195 sketches between November 1922 and September 1923. Two modern wings were added then, and the east gable, largely disintegrated, was rebuilt to a copy of the old Pastorie at Paarl.
dates.note: The grant to Willem Adriaan van der Stel is dated 1700 by every source read. What stands is heavily a 1920s restoration and the record says so rather than letting the 1700 stand alone.

note: Tranche 3, Cape cluster, 5 September 2026. THE ONLY DESCRIBED SAHRA ROW FOR VERGELEGEN IS THE ONE ABOUT THE TREES. The row for the farm itself (9/2/083/0010) carries no description in the table at all; the described sub-record is 9/2/083/0010/001, the five camphor trees, so the survey block quotes the row that exists rather than the row a reader would expect. The Heritage Portal's account is the substantive one and is a secondary work, cited as one: it establishes that the house standing today is Percy Walgate's restoration for Lady Phillips, that two wings were added in the 1920s, and that the east gable is a COPY OF ANOTHER BUILDING'S -- 'the present, rather ornate gable, was copied from the old Pastorie in Paarl'. Anyone measuring a Cape gable from Vergelegen is measuring the Paarl parsonage.
